newsitem.title: UK: Standard Life says banking plans talk speculation.
newsitem.headline: Standard Life says banking plans talk speculation.

text.p: British mutual life assurer Standard Life on Monday described reports that it is about to launch a new banking operation as "pure speculation".
"We haven't announced anything at all and we don't plan to do so in the immediate future," a spokeswoman for the company said.
The opening of services such as savings facilities, personal loans and mortgages would follow similar movess by Prudential Corp and Scottish Widows.
The Financial Times newspaper said an announcement may come within the next ten days.
The aim would be to widen its customer base and capitalise on the opportunities presented by existing clients.
Earlier this year, Jim Spowart joined Standard Life as general manager, banking services from Direct Line.
Spowart oversaw the development of mortgages, loans and savings products while at Direct Line.
